info.title: ImageKit - Image Resize, Convert to WebP, Compress, Crop & EXIF
info.description:
# ImageKit: Image Resize, Convert to WebP, Compress, Crop and EXIF

A simple image-processing API: resize, convert (WebP, JPEG, PNG, GIF, BMP, TIFF, ICO), compress, thumbnail, crop, rotate, grayscale, read EXIF and strip metadata. Point it at an image URL and get the processed image back as bytes or base64.

**Who it's for:** web and app developers, e-commerce and CMS teams, no-code builders and marketers who need image processing without running servers.

## Use cases
- Convert product photos to WebP and cut page weight.
- Generate square avatars and gallery thumbnails on the fly.
- Strip GPS location from user-uploaded photos before publishing.
- Compress images before attaching them to emails or storing them.
- Read camera and date EXIF data for photo-management apps.

## Quickstart
Subscribe on RapidAPI (a free plan is available), copy your key, then:

```bash
curl --request GET \
  --url 'https://imagekit-resize-convert-to-webp-compress-crop.p.rapidapi.com/compress?url=https%3A%2F%2Fupload.wikimedia.org%2Fwikipedia%2Fcommons%2F4%2F47%2FPNG_transparency_demonstration_1.png&output=base64' \
  --header 'X-RapidAPI-Key: YOUR_RAPIDAPI_KEY' \
  --header 'X-RapidAPI-Host: imagekit-resize-convert-to-webp-compress-crop.p.rapidapi.com'
```

## Authentication
Every request goes through RapidAPI. Send `X-RapidAPI-Key` (your key) and `X-RapidAPI-Host` (`imagekit-resize-convert-to-webp-compress-crop.p.rapidapi.com`) on every call. Requests that bypass the gateway are rejected with `403`.

## Good to know
- Source images are read from a public URL (max 15 MB, 40 megapixels, 15 s timeout, redirects not followed).
- Transform endpoints return the image bytes by default; add `output=base64` for JSON with a data URI.
- Animated images are processed as their first frame.

## Rate limits and plans
Request quotas and per-second limits depend on the RapidAPI plan you subscribe to; see the Pricing tab. When a limit is reached the gateway returns `429 Too Many Requests`; retry with exponential backoff or move to a higher plan.

## Errors
All errors are JSON. The API returns `{"error": "<reason>"}` with a meaningful HTTP status: `400` disallowed URL (not http/https, or a private address), `413` input too large, `422` missing or invalid parameter, `502` upstream site or service failed. Gateway errors (`401`/`403`/`429`) come from RapidAPI as `{"message": "<reason>"}`.

## Data sources and licences
- Image processing with Pillow (MIT-CMU licence). Images are processed in memory and not stored.

## MCP (AI agents)
This API is also available as a Model Context Protocol server at `POST /mcp` on the same RapidAPI host; see the MCP endpoint for setup.

get.summary: Get image dimensions, format and EXIF
get.description: Returns format, colour mode, width, height, file size, megapixels, aspect ratio, transparency, animation and frame count, and readable EXIF tags (camera, date, orientation, GPS). The image is not modified.

parameters.name: url
parameters.description: Public http(s) URL of the source image (JPEG, PNG, WebP, GIF, BMP, TIFF or ICO; max 15 MB and 40 megapixels). Redirects are not followed; private addresses are refused.

200.description: Image metadata (this PNG has no EXIF).

413.description: Image larger than 15 MB or 40 megapixels.

422.description: Missing or invalid parameter, or the file is not a supported image.

example.error: Could not read image (supported: JPEG, PNG, WebP, GIF, BMP, TIFF, ICO)

502.description: The image URL could not be fetched or did not return 200.

get.description: Resizes to a width and/or height. Give one side to keep the aspect ratio. `contain` fits inside the box and never enlarges; `cover` fills the box and centre-crops; `fill` stretches to exact size. EXIF orientation is applied first, so phone photos come out the right way up. JPEG output flattens transparency onto white.

parameters.name: url
parameters.description: Public http(s) URL of the source image (JPEG, PNG, WebP, GIF, BMP, TIFF or ICO; max 15 MB and 40 megapixels). Redirects are not followed; private addresses are refused.

parameters.name: width
parameters.description: Target width in px (0-8000). Give width, height or both.

parameters.name: height
parameters.description: Target height in px (0-8000).

parameters.name: fit
parameters.description: Resize mode when both sides are given.

parameters.name: format
parameters.description: Output format. Defaults to the source format.

parameters.name: quality
parameters.description: Lossy quality for JPEG and WebP (clamped to 1-100). Ignored for lossless formats.

parameters.name: output
parameters.description: `binary` returns the image bytes; `base64` returns JSON with a data URI and dimensions.

200.description: The resized image. Binary responses include `X-Image-Width`, `X-Image-Height` and `X-Image-Bytes` headers; with `output=base64` the result is JSON.

413.description: Image larger than 15 MB or 40 megapixels.

422.description: Missing or invalid parameter, or the file is not a supported image.

example.error: Could not read image (supported: JPEG, PNG, WebP, GIF, BMP, TIFF, ICO)

502.description: The image URL could not be fetched or did not return 200.

parameters.description: Lossy quality for JPEG and WebP (clamped to 1-100). Ignored for lossless formats.

get.summary: Compress an image for the web
get.description: Re-encodes the image with optimised settings and optional downscaling to shrink file size for websites and email. Defaults to WebP; set `modern=false` for JPEG (or PNG when the image has transparency). The base64 response includes `original_bytes` so you can show the savings. EXIF orientation is applied first, so phone photos come out the right way up. JPEG output flattens transparency onto white.

parameters.name: url
parameters.description: Public http(s) URL of the source image (JPEG, PNG, WebP, GIF, BMP, TIFF or ICO; max 15 MB and 40 megapixels). Redirects are not followed; private addresses are refused.

parameters.name: quality
parameters.description: Lossy quality for JPEG and WebP (clamped to 1-100). Ignored for lossless formats.

parameters.name: max_width
parameters.description: Downscale images wider than this (px, 0-8000; 0 = keep size). Height follows the aspect ratio.

parameters.name: format
parameters.description: Output format. Overrides `modern`.

parameters.name: modern
parameters.description: When no `format` is given: `true` outputs WebP; `false` outputs JPEG, or PNG for images with transparency.

parameters.name: output
parameters.description: `binary` returns the image bytes; `base64` returns JSON with a data URI and dimensions.

mode.description: Pillow colour mode, e.g. RGB, RGBA, L, P, CMYK.

frames.description: Number of frames (1 for still images).

exif.description: EXIF tags by name (e.g. Make, Model, DateTime, Orientation, GPSInfo). Binary values are omitted, strings cut to 200 chars. Empty when none.
